titulo.texto: At the Foot of the Staircase: Where Coyolxauhqui Appeared

frase_gancho.texto: A stone weighing almost eight tons changed the course of archaeology in the city.

puente_narrativo.texto: Continue along the walkway. When you are ready, move on to the next stop on your tour.

guion_corto.texto: In front of you, at the foot of the south staircase, a stone appeared that changed the history of this place. On February twenty-first, nineteen seventy-eight, workers from the Luz y Fuerza company found a stone disk with a dismembered female figure. It is Coyolxauhqui, and it measures three meters twenty-five centimeters in diameter, according to the INAH. It weighs almost eight tons, and it lay buried for centuries beneath the city. According to the myth, Huitzilopochtli defeated her on the Coatépetl and her body rolled down the slope. That is why the stone was here, at the foot of the god’s sanctuary. The original is now in the museum, just a few steps away.

guion_largo.texto:
You are standing at one of the most important points of the archaeological zone. Here, at the foot of the staircase on the south side, the piece was found that set in motion everything you see.

On February twenty-first, nineteen seventy-eight, workers from the Luz y Fuerza company were doing construction work on this site when they came upon a large stone disk. It was carved with a female figure whose body appeared cut into pieces. The engineer Felipe Curcó Bellet is mentioned in connection with the report. What is clear is that the discovery was accidental and that its importance was understood quickly.

The figure is Coyolxauhqui. Her name, according to the INAH, is translated as she who has bells painted on her face. The disk measures three meters twenty-five centimeters in diameter and weighs almost eight tons. Later, in the museum, you will see the original at your leisure, and you will notice how much detail the relief has.

To understand why it was here, we need to recall the myth. According to Mexica tradition, Coyolxauhqui was the sister of Huitzilopochtli. When he was born on the hill Coatépetl, she and her brothers, the Centzonhuitznahua, wanted to attack their mother, Coatlicue. Huitzilopochtli was born armed, defeated his sister, and her body fell rolling down the slope. The stone represents that moment: the dismembered body at the foot of the mountain.

That is why this place makes sense. The sanctuary of Huitzilopochtli was the Coatépetl, and at the foot of its staircase the scene of the victory was placed. The stone showed the scene of the myth right at the foot of the sacred mountain, so that the building and the story explained each other. It was a way of telling the story without words, to anyone passing through the plaza.

The discovery had enormous consequences. After seeing the disk, it was decided to explore the entire area, and the Templo Mayor Project was created, which worked from nineteen seventy-eight to nineteen eighty-two. The project recovered more than seven thousand objects, which are now part of the museum.

It is striking that the modern city took so long to see what lay beneath it. Manuel Gamio had already found a part of the temple between nineteen thirteen and nineteen fourteen. But it was not until nineteen seventy-eight that this area was explored extensively. More than sixty years passed between one discovery and the other, and in that time the city kept growing on top.

When you go to the museum, look for the hall dedicated to Huitzilopochtli. The original stone is there. Here, by contrast, you can see the place where it once stood. Each visit has its own value: the museum shows the piece up close, and the site shows the setting that gave it meaning. If you can, take both tours at an unhurried pace and compare what you see.

texto.Discovery: February 21, 1978, by Luz y Fuerza workers

texto.pregunta: Myth: Coyolxauhqui was found in a planned archaeological excavation.
texto.respuesta: Reality: It appeared by chance during construction work by Luz y Fuerza, and from that the Templo Mayor Project was born.
